title: Understanding Time Series
text:
A time series is a sequence of observations collected over time, usually at regular intervals.
Examples include:

Daily call-center volume
Monthly sales
Hourly electricity demand
Annual unemployment rates

title: Understanding Time Series
section: Creating a time series in Python
text:
Creating a time series in Python
Let’s create a simple example using pandas.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

dates = pd.date_range(
    start="2026-01-01",
    periods=30,
    freq="D"
)

volume = pd.Series(
    range(100, 130),
    index=dates,
    name="volume"
)

volume.plot(title="Example Daily Volume")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.ylabel("Volume")
plt.show()








This example creates 30 daily observations and plots them over time.

title: Understanding Time Series
text:
Why does time order matter?
Unlike ordinary independent observations, time-series data can contain trends, seasonality, and serial dependence.
Understanding these patterns helps us select appropriate forecasting methods.

section: Learn the concepts, not just the code
text:
Learn the concepts, not just the code
Good forecasting starts with understanding the data. Each tutorial aims to build intuition first, introduce the relevant statistical ideas, and then demonstrate how to apply them in Python.



Foundations
Understand trends, seasonality, stationarity, autocorrelation, and the structure of time-series data.



Statistical forecasting
Explore moving averages, exponential smoothing, ARIMA, SARIMA, and other statistical forecasting methods.






Python in practice
Work through examples using pandas, matplotlib, statsmodels, and scikit-learn, with code that illustrates the ideas being discussed.



Model evaluation
Learn how to compare forecasts, diagnose errors, establish meaningful baselines, and decide which models are useful for a particular problem.

title: Time Series Made Simple
text:
A practical approach to learning
The tutorials follow a consistent progression:

Build intuition. Understand the problem and the patterns in the data.
Explore the theory. Learn the statistical concepts behind the method.
Implement the model. Work through a Python example.
Evaluate the results. Examine forecast accuracy, limitations, and practical trade-offs.

The emphasis is on developing the judgment to choose and evaluate forecasting methods, rather than simply learning how to call a modeling function.
